card.name: Small number words before units
card.fires_on: Number words or first digits (two, one, 3, 6, 4) that start a quantity, right after words like at, approximately, at least or equivalent to. The next word is usually a unit, dose level, or time span.

modes.label: Spelled-out number
modes.description: Words like one or two that begin a quantity such as a dose level or number of weeks.
modes.example: restart at<< one>> dose level lower

modes.label: First digit of a number
modes.description: The leading digit of a two-digit number, often before a unit like minutes, g or mg.
modes.example: wait at least <<3>>0 minutes before eating food

card.writes: It suppresses 'few' and its Chinese equivalents, so it favors an exact number over a vague 'few'.
card.plain: It marks the start of a specific amount, like 'one dose level' or '30 minutes', where the text gives an exact number instead of 'a few'.
